notes: Developmental next-bar-open fill bundle (ADR-0120 accepted). TAF/SEC-31 rates are the MIO plan's illustrative Schwab figures, not live broker pins (§11 item 9 remains open). Spread (owner ruling 2026-09-25, ADR-0120/0185 amendment): each side pays the name's QUOTED half-spread (half_spread_bps, bp) x eq_ratio (the broker's effective/quoted ratio). Provenance, tools/spread-cost-results.json (window 2024-11-01..2026-02-27, reads nothing at or after 2026-02-28): LLY/XOM/JPM are MEASURED all-minute medians of the minute NBBO (symbols.*.half_spread_bps.all.median; JPM partial, 99 sessions); XLK/LRCX/NOW/PANW/ADBE/MSTR/TER/LULU/CIEN/LITE are the MODELLED medians (cohort.*.predicted_half_spread_bps: log hs on log price, log $vol, log 1-min sigma over 759 name-days, floored at 0.5c/price; indicative, three training names); LLY uses its measured 4.51 over its modelled 4.47. All rounded to 0.01 bp. default_half_spread_bps 5.62 is the cohort maximum (LITE), a conservative charge for any unlisted name. eq_ratio 0.25 (plausible range 0.10-0.40) is a PROXY, not Schwab's own figure: HRT's Rule 605 report for July 2026 (https://public.s3.com/rule605/hrtf/THRTF202607.dat), 100-499-share S&P 500 market orders, gives E/Q ~0.25 overall and 0.16-0.24 for the cohort names (LLY 0.36); HRT takes ~8% of Schwab's S&P 500 market-order flow (Schwab Rule 606 Q1 2026; Citadel 42.5%); Fidelity self-reports ~0.25; Schwarz et al. (JF 2025) measured TD Ameritrade tiny orders at ~0.06. PENDING: replace with Schwab's own amended Rule 605 figure (first report due end of Sep 2026 at public.s3.com/rule605/chas/), then validate against live fills. Time of day (owner ruling 2026-09-25, option B, ADR-0120/0185 amendment): spread_time_of_day multiplies the quoted half-spread by the window of the FILL minute (the replay's fill bar = decision bar + fill_bar_offset), in BOTH EquityKellyMIO sizing (portfolio.fill_ms) and the replay's fills, so both charge the identical per-share rate. Windows are America/New_York wall-clock minutes after midnight, half-open [start, end), DST-aware; a minute in no window pays default_multiplier 1.0. Provenance, same file: each multiplier is the median over the three measured names (LLY/XOM/JPM) of that bucket's median quoted half-spread divided by the all-minute median (the base half_spread_bps is itself an all-minute median), rounded to 0.01: open30 [570, 600) 09:30-10:00 = 1.84 (LLY 1.70, XOM 1.84, JPM 2.02); close30 [930, 960) 15:30-16:00 = 0.62 (LLY 0.65, XOM 0.59, JPM 0.62). The research note's '~2x / ~0.65x' is relative to MIDDAY; midday is 0.89-1.00 of the all-minute median, hence 1.0 elsewhere. The modelled names are assumed to share the measured names' intraday shape. Changing a value here moves identity; never copy these numbers into Python.
